references.text: The Sabbath commandment in the Ten Commandments, where God commands keeping the seventh day holy as a day of rest, based on the pattern of creation.
The Sabbath is described as a holy day of rest on which no work shall be done.
Moses repeats the Sabbath commandment to the people and emphasizes that the seventh day must be a holy day of rest.
God rested on the seventh day after creation and sanctified it, forming the basis for Sabbath rest.
The Sabbath commandment is repeated in Deuteronomy with emphasis on rest for the entire household and remembrance of the exodus from Egypt.
The book of Hebrews interprets Sabbath rest as a picture of the spiritual rest awaiting God's people.
The people's Sabbath in the wilderness is a direct imitation of and participation in God's creation rest from Genesis 2.
The book of Hebrews uses the creation rest (referred to in Exodus 16) as a theological foundation for proclaiming a future, eternal Sabbath rest.
Genesis 2:3 provides the theological justification (God's blessing and rest) for why the people in Exodus keep the seventh day holy.
The book of Hebrews confirms that the Sabbath rest introduced in Exodus remains a living promise for God's people.
Numbers 28:25 formalizes and confirms the practical implementation of Sabbath rest that occurred in Exodus 16.
